question.text: Under FATCA and CRS, AIFs as Reporting Financial Institutions must comply with which Indian tax rules and register with which authority?

answer.text: Rules 114F-114H of the Income Tax Rules, 1962; register with US IRS for GIIN AND with Indian Income Tax authorities
Rule 10 of FEMA; register only with RBI
Rule 20 of SEBI ICDR; register with SEBI only

explanation.text: The Logic: FATCA (US Internal Revenue Code) and CRS (OECD Common Reporting Standard) compliance for AIFs is operationalised in India via Rules 114F to 114H of the Income Tax Rules, 1962. AIFs must register with the US IRS to obtain a GIIN (Global Intermediary Identification Number) AND with the Indian Income Tax authorities. Mandatory self-declaration from all Indian and NRI investors from January 2016. FATCA for 'U.S. persons', CRS for foreign investors from other signatory countries. The Trap: Options B/C/D cite wrong regulatory frameworks. FEMA/SEBI/MCA don't house FATCA-CRS — Income Tax Rules do. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests FATCA/CRS. XXIV AML interlinks with reporting obligations. X-A/B Investment Adviser also tests FATCA for client-side reporting. Manager's Pro-Tip: FATCA GIIN is a one-time registration but renewable every 3 years. Maintain investor self-declarations (FATCA + CRS) in the subscription documents. If LP refuses to provide FATCA self-declaration, you can reject or redeem existing units — make this contractual in Contribution Agreement.
